findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the combined candidate ordering across all three sources (fenced blocks, balanced objects, array-unwrap) and specify de-duplication of identical candidates, so 'first'/'last' for last-valid-wins and the AC #2 '>=2 validate and last != first' warning are deterministic (e.g. a fence-wrapped verdict counts once).
evidence: Plan lists sources as 'every fenced block … every top-level non-overlapping balanced object (cap: keep the LAST 32), plus the array-unwrap forms' but never states their combined ordering, which alone determines first/last.
Winner rule is order-sensitive: 'the LAST valid candidate wins' and 'when >=2 validate and last != first, log a warning'.

In the codebase, tolerant_parse already treats a fenced group and the raw text as overlapping candidate sources (structured.py:137-150), and _first_json_object (:82) scans balanced objects in the raw text — so a fence-wrapped verdict is scannable both as a fenced block and as a top-level balanced object, producing two identical candidates.
AC #2 pins the warning ('>=2 candidates validate and last != first') without defining how identical duplicate survivors are counted or ordered.
findings.finding: The candidate-set enumeration order across the three sources (fenced blocks, top-level balanced objects capped at LAST 32, array-unwrap forms) is not pinned, and duplicate candidates are not de-duplicated — a fenced block's inner object is ALSO enumerable as a top-level balanced object, so the same payload can appear twice; both leave 'first' vs 'last' under the last-valid-wins rule and the '>=2 validate and last != first' warning ambiguous.
findings.location: Plan 'Approach' — 'Selection: enumerate candidates … the LAST valid candidate wins; when >=2 validate and last != first, log a warning naming both'; AC #2
scenarios: A model fence-wraps its single real verdict (the plan's stated common case: 'models fence-wrap quoted records'); the identical object is enumerated as both a fenced candidate and a top-level balanced-object candidate, so >=2 'validate' and the last-wins warning fires spuriously on one true object.

A reply with one decoy dep-record and one fenced verdict: whether the verdict is 'last' (and wins) depends on the unpinned cross-source ordering, so the winner and the AC #2 warning behavior are not deterministic from the spec.
findings.suggested_fix: State the enumeration order explicitly (e.g. raw-text balanced objects in document order, then fenced-block contents, then array-unwrap forms), de-duplicate candidates by parsed-value equality before screening, and define 'first'/'last' over that de-duplicated ordered list; add a test that a single fence-wrapped verdict validates without triggering the >=2-validate warning.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate parse_structured's consumers (or state there are none beyond the verifier) and confirm the first->last-valid-wins flip is safe for each, acknowledging it as a deliberate behavior change.
evidence: 'Known residual, accepted: against an all-defaults contract, a late single-shared-key decoy can validate and win under last-wins'
tolerant_parse's first-wins is pinned, but parse_structured's own consumers are not enumerated
findings.finding: The plan flips parse_structured's selection from first-object-wins to last-valid-wins, but only analyzes the impact on the completion verifier; it does not enumerate other parse_structured consumers or confirm the first->last-wins change is safe (or acknowledged-breaking) for them.
scenarios: A different contract/caller currently relying on parse_structured returning the FIRST valid object for a multi-object reply silently gets a different (last) object after this change.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a scope note listing parse_structured callers and a one-line rationale that last-valid-wins does not regress them (single-object replies are unaffected; the change only bites multi-valid-candidate replies, which are the injection case).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the last-valid-wins + schema-screen selection rationale (including the >=1-key threshold and LAST-32 cap) in a code docstring/comment or design-doc note so it survives beyond the ticket.
evidence: 'a candidate survives iff the set intersection ... is non-empty (>= 1 shared key)'
No mention of ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc capture for the new selection algorithm
findings.finding: The schema-screen threshold (>=1 shared key) and the LAST-32 candidate cap are hardcoded constants with no note on where they live or whether they are tunable; a novel selection algorithm added to a shared pipeline stage has no ADR/AGENTS.md capture beyond the plan prose.
findings.location: Approach — 'keep the LAST 32' and '>= 1 shared key' threshold
scenarios: A future maintainer needs to understand why last-valid-wins + >=1-key-screen + last-32-cap were chosen and cannot find the rationale outside this ticket.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate structured_run.py:213 as the shared production consumer of parse_structured and state that the first-wins→last-valid-wins selection change applies to ALL registered contracts (naming which out-of-dir callers are unaffected because they feed single-object input).
evidence: Scope lists only 'src/rebar/llm/structured.py — candidate selection in parse_structured', 'tests/unit/test_structured.py', 'tests/fixtures/'
src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:213 `parsed = structured.parse_structured(str(result.output), model_cls)` is the sole production caller and passes model_cls for ALL registered contracts

Other out-of-dir callers (tests/unit/test_review_kernel.py:354-362, tests/unit/test_silent_success.py:88) feed single-object inputs, where first-wins vs last-valid-wins is identical — so they are genuinely unaffected and need no edit; the point is enumeration completeness, not a missing edit
Negative control names only test_structured.py ('the full existing tests/unit/test_structured.py suite passes unmodified')
findings.finding: The plan's Scope and Testing sections do not enumerate structured_run.py:213 — the single production runtime consumer of parse_structured through which EVERY structured contract flows — even though the change flips parse_structured's multi-candidate selection from first-wins to last-valid-wins for all contracts, not just CompletionVerdict.
scenarios: A non-CompletionVerdict contract (e.g. the findings model or a review-kernel contract) whose real reply contains multiple parseable objects now resolves via last-valid-wins instead of first-wins, silently changing which object is validated in the production path
A reviewer/implementer confirming no regression across all contracts has no explicit pointer to the shared production entry point
findings.suggested_fix: In Scope, add a consumer note: 'parse_structured is the single production entry point (structured_run.py:213) for every registered contract; this change alters its multi-candidate selection for all of them. Out-of-dir callers test_review_kernel.py and test_silent_success.py feed single-object inputs and are behaviorally unaffected.' Extend the negative-control AC to assert the review-kernel and silent-success parse pins also pass unmodified.
